title: Fix the short-trip charge
prompt: A trip is charged at least 7.00 on the meter, plus its surcharge. The function below was written for the charge report, but it fails, and its idea of a minimum is wrong too. Fix `solve(trips)`.
rules: Return three columns, in this order: `trip_id`, `fare` and `charged`.
`charged` is the larger of `fare` and 7.00, plus `surcharge`, as a `decimal(9,2)`: a fare of 5.00 with a 0.50 surcharge is charged 7.50, a fare of 16.38 is charged 16.88.
A missing fare counts as under the minimum: it's charged 7.00 plus its surcharge. A missing surcharge gives a missing charge. Keep every trip, duplicates included.
hints: Press Run and read the error: Spark tried to turn the text `surcharge` into a number.
A plain string next to `+` is a value, not a column. Write `F.col("surcharge")`.
`F.least` picks the smaller value, which makes 7.00 a cap. A minimum needs the larger of the two: `F.greatest`.
explanation: Two bugs. `+ "surcharge"` adds the text `surcharge`, not the column, and Spark 4 stops when it can't turn that text into a number; it must be `F.col("surcharge")`. Then `F.least("fare", minimum)` picks the smaller value, so every fare above 7.00 is cut down to 7.00: that's a cap, not a minimum. A minimum is `F.greatest("fare", minimum)`. Fixed: `(F.greatest("fare", F.lit(Decimal("7.00"))) + F.col("surcharge")).alias("charged")`, which is already a `decimal(9,2)`. A fare of exactly 7.00 is charged 7.00 either way.
